extracted.intended_audience: Authors, illustrators, publishers, and nominators submitting children's and young adult books (especially African American creators) for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for submitting and evaluating children's and YA books for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards (authors and illustrators) and the John Steptoe New Talent Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — encourage artistic expression of African American experience
rubrics_metrics.description: To encourage the artistic expression of the African American experience via literature and the graphic arts, including biographical, historical and social history treatments by African American authors and illustrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is designed to promote works that express aspects of the African American experience across genres and forms; this purpose frames eligibility and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of understanding and pluralism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Coretta Scott King Book Award titles promote understanding and appreciation of the cultures of all peoples and their contribution to the realization of the American dream of a pluralistic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles should foster appreciation of diverse cultures and support the values of a pluralistic society; commemorating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and honoring Mrs. Coretta Scott King are central to the award's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of the Black experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Must portray some aspect of the black experience, past, present, or future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should explicitly engage with elements of Black life, history, culture, identity, or future perspectives; this is a core content requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator identity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be written/illustrated by an African American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only works by African American authors or illustrators are eligible for the primary Coretta Scott King author and illustrator awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and place
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be published in the U.S. in the year preceding presentation of the Award. (For example: only books published in 2023 will qualify for the 2024 award.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to U.S.-published books whose copyright/publication date falls in the specified calendar year immediately before the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be an original work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be original publications (not translations or previously published editions that would disqualify originality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing — clear plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Must meet established standards of quality writing for youth which include: Clear plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative clarity and coherent plot structure appropriate to the intended age group are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing — character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Must meet established standards of quality writing for youth which include: Well drawn characters, which portray growth and development during the course of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters should be fully realized and demonstrate development over the course of the work; static or flat characterization is a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing — age-appropriate style
rubrics_metrics.description: Must meet established standards of quality writing for youth which include: Writing style which is consistent with and suitable to the age intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone, vocabulary, sentence structure, and thematic complexity should match the targeted readership (Preschool–Grade 4, Grades 5–8, Grades 9–12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing — accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Must meet established standards of quality writing for youth which include: Accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual correctness (where applicable) and fidelity to historical/cultural detail are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience category
rubrics_metrics.description: Must be written for a youth audience in one of three categories: Preschool–grade 4; Grades 5–8; Grades 9–12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must identify the intended age/grade category; judging occurs within these audience groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic/moral impact — motivation toward citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular attention will be paid to titles which seek to motivate readers to develop their own attitudes and behaviors as well as comprehend their personal duty and responsibility as citizens in a pluralistic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that encourage ethical reflection, civic responsibility, and constructive attitudes toward diversity will be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustration standards (Cianciolo guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should... 'heighten and extend the readers' awareness of the world around him. They should lead him to an appreciation of beauty. The style and content of the illustrations should be...neither coy nor condescending...Storytelling qualities should enlarge upon the story elements that were hinted in the text and should include details that will awaken and strengthen the imagination of the reader and permit him to interpret the words and pictures in a manner unique to him' (Cianciolo, Illustrations in Children's Books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations should enhance and expand the text, avoid patronizing tones, contribute to storytelling, stimulate imagination, and allow individual interpretation; technical skill and aesthetic quality are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residency/citizenship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Author or illustrator must live in the U.S. or maintain dual residency/citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators must have U.S. residence or dual status; this is an eligibility filter rather than an artistic criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Book must be published in the year preceding the year the award is given, evidenced by the copyright date printed in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters must ensure the book's copyright/publication date falls within the eligible window and is verifiable in the submitted copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finished copies only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only finished copies will be accepted. Do not send advance reader copies, galleys, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-publication materials or proofs are ineligible; judges review final printed editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-return of submitted titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles submitted for the Coretta Scott King Book Awards will not be returned. Titles received by the ODLOS office are donated as part of The Coretta Scott King Books Awards Donation Grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should not expect return of physical copies; plan donation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: John Steptoe Award — same selection criteria with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for eligibility will be the same as those for the writing and illustration awards, with the exception that the winner(s)' published works cannot exceed three in number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: John Steptoe recognizes new talent; eligible creators must meet the Coretta criteria and additionally be early in their publishing careers (no more than three published works).

rubrics_metrics.name: John Steptoe Award — exclusion for concurrent Coretta winners
rubrics_metrics.description: An author or illustrator who has already received or has just been selected to win one of the Coretta Scott King Book Awards in the current year is not eligible for the John Steptoe Award for New Talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators receiving Coretta recognition in the same award cycle cannot also receive the John Steptoe New Talent Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: John Steptoe Award — one-time eligibility and award discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may receive this award one time. One award will be presented annually for text or illustrations. The committee may choose to select one book for writing and a second book for illustration. The award need not be given if the committee so decides in a particular year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The John Steptoe Award is limited to a single receipt per author; selection is discretionary and may be split or withheld in a given year.
